title: Approve an effective, reversible non-hormonal male contraceptive drug

concept.text: Prevent pregnancy through a pharmacological effect on sperm production or function without administering sex hormones. YCT-529 has human phase 1 safety data, but that study did not establish contraceptive efficacy. Proposed completion test: FDA approval following a pivotal couples study with at least 500 couple-years of exposure, fewer than 2 pregnancies per 100 couple-years, acceptable systemic safety, and recovery of fertility after stopping treatment. Test set by: FDA would decide approval; WHO's 2026 TPP supplies the product-development framework. The numerical exposure and efficacy thresholds are editorial proposals. Sources given: [WHO male contraceptive target product profiles](https://www.who.int/publications/i/item/9789240124950) ; [YCT-529 first-in-human safety study](https://www.nature.com/articles/s43856-025-01004-4.pdf).

page.title: Reversible non-hormonal male contraceptive drug
page.definition: An approved drug administered to men would prevent pregnancy by suppressing sperm production or disabling sperm function without administering sex hormones. Fertility would recover after treatment stops.

goal.need: An estimated 121.0 million unintended pregnancies occurred annually worldwide in 2015–2019 (80% uncertainty interval, 112.8–131.5 million). Existing male methods include condoms and vasectomy; FDA describes vasectomy as surgery for men who do not want future children and warns that reversal may fail.

figures.caption: Pregnancies expected during one year of contraceptive use
figures.note: FDA describes these figures as actual-use estimates, including incorrect or inconsistent use.

statements.quote: To expand men's contraceptive choices, efforts are underway to develop safe, effective and reversible novel male contraceptive methods and delivery systems.
statements.context: The publication introduces target product profiles covering suppression of sperm production, inhibition of sperm function and blockade of sperm transport.

statements.context: A specific objective under the branch's contraceptive research and development programme.

completion.title: FDA approves a drug for reversible non-hormonal male contraception.
completion.criterion: FDA grants marketing approval through a New Drug Application for a drug administered to men to prevent pregnancy without administering sex hormones. The approved use and reviewed human evidence support a reversible contraceptive effect. FDA finds effectiveness for the proposed use, benefits that outweigh risks, appropriate labeling and adequate manufacturing quality.
completion.set_by: US Food and Drug Administration, New Drug Application review criteria; reversibility is part of the intended use specified here.
completion.threshold_quote: Whether the drug is safe and effective in its proposed use(s), and whether the benefits of the drug outweigh the risks.
completion.basis: Marketing approval is the externally adjudicated test for the requested approved capability. The andrology societies also require confirmation of reversibility in initial human studies. WHO's target product profiles guide development and regulatory review; they do not themselves authorize marketing.

milestones.title: A non-hormonal male drug produces reversible contraception in animal mating studies.
milestones.criterion: Animal studies establish contraceptive action, reversibility, mechanism, pharmacological effects and toxicology. YCT-529 results published on 13 March 2025: after 10 mg/kg/day orally for 4 weeks, 13/15 male mice produced no pregnancies during 2-week matings begun one day after withdrawal; 9/10 assessed 6 weeks after withdrawal had recovered fertility. TDI-11861 results published on 14 February 2023: after a 50 mg/kg injection, pregnancies occurred in 0/52 pairings at 0.5–2.5 hours and 13/15 recovery pairings begun 24 hours after dosing and lasting 4 days.
milestones.set_by: European Academy of Andrology and American Society of Andrology (EAA/ASA), recommendations 48–49 in the recommendation table.

milestones.title: A non-hormonal male contraceptive drug is administered in an authorized first-in-human study.
milestones.criterion: An investigational non-hormonal male contraceptive is administered in an authorized phase 1 study. YCT-529's MHRA-authorized study enrolled 16 vasectomized men, aged 32–59 years, and evaluated single oral doses of 10–180 mg. It finished on 18 June 2024; results appeared on 22 July 2025. No severe or serious treatment-emergent adverse events were reported; one participant had transient asymptomatic arrhythmia considered possibly drug-related.
milestones.set_by: US Food and Drug Administration, definition of phase 1 clinical studies; the cited YCT-529 study was authorized by the UK Medicines and Healthcare products Regulatory Agency.
milestones.threshold_quote: Phase 1 includes the initial introduction of an investigational new drug into humans.

milestones.title: A male drug suppresses sperm production or function in a 6-month study, with recovery after withdrawal.
milestones.criterion: Human studies establish when sperm production or function is suppressed over 6 months and confirm recovery after withdrawal. Each product needs its own semen threshold. YCT-529's published single-dose study did not assess sperm parameters or fertility recovery.
milestones.set_by: EAA/ASA, recommendations 49–50 for non-hormonal male contraceptive agents.
milestones.threshold_quote: We suggest documenting the time to suppressing spermatogenesis or sperm function in a 6-month study.

milestones.title: Couples complete 1 year using a non-hormonal male drug as their only contraceptive.
milestones.criterion: Couples complete 1 year using only the male drug, with at least one vaginal intercourse episode per menstrual cycle. Monthly pregnancy follow-up establishes the Kaplan–Meier 1-year pregnancy probability and 95% confidence interval. Recommendation 52 supplies no universal numerical success cutoff.
milestones.set_by: EAA/ASA, recommendation 52 and its exposure conditions, presented in the recommendation table.

milestones.title: About 1,500 men receive a male drug, including 300–600 for 6 months and 100 for 1 year.
milestones.criterion: For a drug intended for chronic or repeated intermittent use beyond 6 months, about 1,500 individuals receive the drug in clinical development, including 300–600 treated for 6 months and at least 100 for 1 year at intended clinical doses. ICH E1 permits exceptions according to risk; the andrology societies apply this framework to non-hormonal male contraceptives.
milestones.set_by: International Conference on Harmonisation, ICH E1, paragraphs 4–7; applied to non-hormonal male contraception by EAA/ASA recommendation 51.
milestones.threshold_quote: It is anticipated that the total number of individuals treated with the investigational drug, including short-term exposure, will be about 1500.

milestones.title: FDA accepts a non-hormonal male contraceptive drug's marketing application for substantive review.
milestones.criterion: FDA accepts the drug's New Drug Application for substantive review under 21 CFR 314.101(a), finding it sufficiently complete. The application contains the nonclinical, clinical, manufacturing and proposed-labeling evidence supporting reversible non-hormonal male contraception.
milestones.set_by: US Food and Drug Administration, 21 CFR 314.101(a)(1).
milestones.threshold_quote: FDA has made a threshold determination that the NDA is sufficiently complete to permit a substantive review.

not_found: WHO's final report published on 22 September 2026 could not be opened from IRIS, so its numerical targets could not be verified.
Searches of FDA guidance found no male-drug-specific numerical approval cutoff for pregnancy prevention or fertility recovery.
Searches of YCT-529 publications found no human fertility-recovery or couples pregnancy-efficacy results.
ClinicalTrials.gov pages did not render detailed study records.

Triptonide is a reversible non-hormonal male contraceptive agent in mice and non-human primates

results.finding: YCT-529 suppressed fertility in male mice: 13 of 15 produced no pregnancies during mating.
results.detail: After 10 mg/kg/day orally for four weeks, mating began one day after treatment stopped. By six weeks after treatment, 9 of 10 assessed mice had regained fertility. The study also reports disrupted spermatogenesis, pharmacokinetics and toxicology findings.
results.quote: At one day post-CDT, 13 out of 15 drug-treated males failed to yield pregnancies after mating for 2 weeks

results.finding: TDI-11861 prevented pregnancy in 52 of 52 mouse mating pairings.
results.detail: After a 50 mg/kg injection, pairings ran from 0.5 to 2.5 hours. In recovery matings begun 24 hours after injection and lasting 4 days, 93% of pairings yielded litters. The study also examined mechanism, pharmacology and toxicology.

results.finding: Triptonide: 0 of 32 females paired with 16 treated male mice became pregnant.
results.detail: Fertility recovered after treatment stopped, and the study examined sperm effects and toxicity. However, the proposed molecular mechanism needs validation, and the authors say comprehensive pharmacokinetic and toxicology studies are needed.
results.quote: All 16 male mice tested (8 in each group) became infertile after 4 weeks, and infertility persisted between week 4 and the third or sixth month of treatment, as evidenced by the fact that none of the 32 fertile adult females placed into the individually housed, treated male mice (2 females per male) became pregnant.

results.finding: YCT-529 was administered in a first-in-human phase 1a study enrolling 16 men, with single oral doses of 10–180 mg.
results.detail: The study had MHRA and ethics committee approval and was completed on 18 June 2024. No severe or serious treatment-emergent adverse events were reported; one participant had transient asymptomatic arrhythmia considered possibly drug-related. Sperm parameters were not assessed.
results.quote: A phase 1a first-in-human trial evaluated single oral ascending-doses (SAD) of YCT-529 (10–180 mg) in 16 healthy males across 2 cohorts.
